fields.claim_type: water use and cooling for the Thane facility
fields.notes: First-party AWS page dated by its 27 May 2026 tree-report reference. Supersedes secondary 0.01 MLD myth-buster figure (FPJ 18 Jul 2026); 125 KLD is about 0.125 MLD. Summary used for the title; verbatim is the page text.

records.verbatim: The total water use at our Thane facility will be 125 kilolitres per day (KLD). 115 KLD is treated sewage water for landscaping and irrigation, supplied by the Thane Municipal Council (TMC). We will use closed-loop cooling technology to cool our Thane data center.

fields.notes: Dedicated 'very own' HV substation; grid isolation from residential distribution is the company's own assertion, and the Thane site is under resident protest (see leads). Record as a company claim, not a finding.

records.verbatim: Our Thane data center will not draw electricity from the local distribution network that supplies homes, shops and businesses. Instead, we are on an industrial connection to the high-voltage transmission grid, and have established our very own dedicated high-voltage substation, planned in coordination with the utility.

fields.notes: National, not site-specific: AWS says its operational Indian sites use no water for cooling. Pair with the Thane site's planned closed-loop cooling claim. Not a Thane fact. Page gives no publication date.

records.verbatim: None of Amazon's operational data centres in India use any water for cooling as it uses air-cooled chillers. We take utmost care to ensure that our data centres do not draw or divert power from the local distribution grid that serves residents.

fields.notes: Mumbai-region community programme, not tied to one site. Figures are AWS's own. Named students and officials on the page are not repeated here.

records.verbatim: Amazon operates 55 Think Big Spaces reaching 12,000+ public school students annually. Amazon has helped upskill over 230 youth for jobs in the data centre and IT/ITeS sector, with over 70% being offered jobs at Amazon and other companies.

fields.name: CoreWeave campus at AdaniConneX Taloja, Navi Mumbai
fields.notes: Host and developer: AdaniConneX (50:50 Adani Enterprises / EdgeConneX). CoreWeave is sole tenant of three 80 MW buildings; option to double to 480 MW. First phase mid-2028. Adani's own campus table lists Navi Mumbai at 1,000 MW planned from Dec 2026, not reconciled (see leads). Release date: 6 Oct 2026 dateline / 7 Oct on investor site. COO Sachin Jain quoted. Gate 2 note: CoreWeave is a tracked company that already signed the pledge; this is a project record only.

records.verbatim: CoreWeave plans to expand its AI Cloud platform with 240 megawatts (MW) of data center capacity in Navi Mumbai. The new campus will span three 80 MW buildings at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus. CoreWeave will be the sole tenant across the three buildings, with the opportunity to double capacity by expanding by up to 240 MW at the campus. The first phase of the project is expected to be available in mid-2028

leads: AdaniConneX campus table (adaniconnex.com/data-centers, first-party): Chennai 33 MW (Phase 1 Oct 2022), Hyderabad 600 MW (Phase 1 live Oct 2024), Navi Mumbai 1,000 MW planned (Dec 2026), Noida 150 MW (Phase 1 live Jan 2025), Pune 250 MW (listed 'Phase 1 Live: Oct 2025' but described as 'soon to be launched' on the same page, contradictory), Visakhapatnam 1 GW planned (Dec 2028). The 2023 financing covered 67 MW across Chennai and Noida. Table figures are not in quotable sentences, so they are not probe-verified. Reconcile before filing AdaniConneX project records. Adani project records need a dated per-site announcement first.
